title: Red Hat Certified Technologist in OpenShift Virtualization
description: Unofficial knowledge practice for EX156 (OpenShift Virtualization on OpenShift Container Platform 4.18). Mapped to Red Hat's published exam objectives. The real exam is a 2-hour performance-based lab with product docs only; these items are not Red Hat exam questions.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: In the OpenShift web console, which path opens the instance-type catalog used to create a virtual machine?
questions.explanation: OpenShift Virtualization’s create flow lives under Virtualization → Catalog. The InstanceTypes tab is the default; Template catalog is a separate tab. Compute MachineSets are infrastructure, not guest VMs.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: You want only templates that already have a disk image. Which catalog filter should you enable?
questions.explanation: The Template catalog includes a Boot source available checkbox so you see templates that already have a bootable volume. Templates without a source are labeled Boot source required.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: You selected a template with an available boot source and do not need to change disks, cloud-init, or SSH keys. Which action creates the VM immediately?
questions.explanation: Quick create VirtualMachine provisions from the template without opening the customize wizard. Customize VirtualMachine is for editing Overview, YAML, Network interfaces, Disks, and Scripts first.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: A running VM was created from an instance type. Where in the web console do you change that instance type so the new size takes effect immediately?

choices.text: VirtualMachine details → Configuration → Details, then the instance type text

questions.explanation: On VirtualMachine details, the Configuration tab’s Details view shows the current instance type (for example 1 CPU | 2 GiB Memory). Editing Series and Size updates the VM immediately.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: When you create a VM from an instance type, you can override the CPU and memory values defined in that instance type on the VirtualMachine spec.
questions.explanation: Instance types require cpu and memory. OpenShift Virtualization rejects extra requests for those resources on a VM created from an instance type; those parameters cannot be overridden.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two custom resources define reusable VM instance types? Select two.
questions.explanation: OpenShift Virtualization ships namespaced VirtualMachineInstancetype and cluster-wide VirtualMachineClusterInstancetype, both using VirtualMachineInstancetypeSpec. MachineSet is the OpenShift node API; HyperConverged is the operator config.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: The pre-defined general-purpose instance type u1.medium provides which resources?

choices.text: 1 vCPU and 4 GiB memory (1:4 ratio, burstable CPU)

questions.explanation: The U (general purpose) series uses burstable CPU and a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. u1.medium is 1 vCPU and 4 GiB. N/CX/M series have different ratios and hugepage/dedicated-CPU traits.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: What is the Kubernetes kind of the primary guest object you apply with oc to define a VM in OpenShift Virtualization? Enter the kind only.
questions.explanation: Guests are kubevirt.io/v1 VirtualMachine objects. A running instance is a VirtualMachineInstance created from the VM template spec.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: What apiVersion is used on a VirtualMachine manifest in current OpenShift Virtualization documentation?
questions.explanation: Documented VM YAML uses apiVersion kubevirt.io/v1 and kind VirtualMachine.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which command writes a VirtualMachine manifest you can pipe to oc apply?

choices.text: oc create -f vm.yaml after hand-writing a Pod spec named rhel9

questions.explanation: virtctl create vm generates a VM manifest, including volume-import from a DataSource in openshift-virtualization-os-images. oc new-app, podman, and virt-install are not the OpenShift Virtualization create path.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which virtctl subcommand starts a stopped virtual machine? Enter the subcommand only (not the VM name).
questions.explanation: virtctl start <vm_name> starts a VM. stop, restart, pause, unpause, and migrate are separate management commands.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two virtctl commands manage power without deleting the VirtualMachine object? Select two.
questions.explanation: start and stop change run state. oc delete vm removes the object. virtctl vmexport delete removes a VirtualMachineExport, not the guest.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: How does virtctl pause differ from virtctl stop?

choices.text: Pause keeps the machine state in memory; stop shuts the guest down.
Pause deletes the VirtualMachineInstance; stop does not.
Pause is only available in the web console.
Stop keeps RAM contents; pause always writes a snapshot.

questions.explanation: virtctl pause vm keeps machine state in memory. unpause resumes it. stop performs a shutdown (force stop with --grace-period 0 --force can lose data). Pause does not create a disk snapshot.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: On RHEL 8, after enabling the cnv-4.18 repository, which RPM package installs the virtctl client?
questions.explanation: RHEL 8 uses subscription-manager to enable cnv-4.18-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms, then yum install kubevirt-virtctl. On RHEL 9 and other OSes you download the virtctl binary from Virtualization → Overview.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which virtctl command attaches to a Linux guest’s serial console?
questions.explanation: virtctl console connects to the serial console. virtctl vnc is the graphical console (needs virt-viewer). oc rsh talks to containers, not KubeVirt serial.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: You need a VM manifest that injects cloud-init user fedora and an SSH public key. Which virtctl pattern is documented for that?

choices.text: virtctl create vm --name web1 --user fedora --ssh-key='ssh-ed25519 AAAA…'

questions.explanation: virtctl create vm --user <name> --ssh-key|password-file=<value> adds cloud-init that creates the user and installs the key or password. virtctl ssh is for connecting later, not for baking the key into the manifest.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two virtctl flags explicitly infer sizing and OS preference from the boot volume? Select two.
questions.explanation: --infer-instancetype and --infer-preference read labels on the boot volume (or --infer-*-from another volume). Inference is on by default with Ignore-on-failure unless flags force Reject.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What is the recommended binding method for a VM NIC attached to the default pod network?
questions.explanation: Masquerade (NAT) is the recommended and supported binding for the default pod network. Bridge and SR-IOV are for secondary/predefined networks. Masquerade is not supported on non-default networks.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: The masquerade binding method is supported for secondary (non-default) networks attached through Multus.
questions.explanation: Documentation states masquerade is not supported for non-default networks. Secondary Linux-bridge networks use bridge; SR-IOV networks use the SR-IOV binding.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: A VM must sit on an existing VLAN presented as a Linux bridge NAD. Which interface binding should that NIC use?
questions.explanation: Linux bridge NADs attach with the bridge binding. A Linux bridge NAD is the usual way to put a VM on a VLAN. ClusterIP is a Service type, not a NIC binding.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What Kubernetes kind (from the Multus CRD) exposes a layer-2 device in a namespace so a VM can attach to it?
questions.explanation: NetworkAttachmentDefinition (k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1) is the Multus object that publishes a CNI network in a namespace. VM spec.networks[].multus.networkName points at it.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: Which custom resource kind creates a namespace-scoped OVN user-defined network that can replace the default pod network?
questions.explanation: UserDefinedNetwork (k8s.ovn.org/v1) is namespace-scoped. ClusterUserDefinedNetwork is the cluster-scoped shared overlay. Namespaces that use a primary UDN need the k8s.ovn.org/primary-user-defined-network label.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: Which label must you add when creating a namespace that will use a primary user-defined network?
questions.explanation: The namespace must have k8s.ovn.org/primary-user-defined-network. Then a UserDefinedNetwork CR with role Primary can replace the default pod network in that namespace.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: A primary user-defined network with layer2 topology can keep a VM IP address across live migration and reboot, without NAT.
questions.explanation: Layer2 UDN overlay is documented as a good VM alternative to secondary networks: seamless migration without NAT and persistent IPs across reboot and live migration.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What does a primary user-defined network do for VMs in the labeled namespace?

choices.text: It replaces the default pod network on the VM’s primary interface.
It adds a secondary Multus NIC beside the unchanged default pod network.
It creates a Linux-bridge NAD named default in every namespace.
It attaches an SR-IOV VF as the only VM interface.

questions.explanation: A primary UDN replaces the default pod network for pods and VMs in selected namespaces, isolating the tenant without requiring NetworkPolicy.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: Which object creates a shared OVN layer2 network that multiple namespaces can use?
questions.explanation: Cluster administrators use ClusterUserDefinedNetwork for a shared OVN layer2 network across namespaces. UserDefinedNetwork is namespace-scoped.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: OpenShift Virtualization supports which two OVN-Kubernetes topologies for a secondary VM network? Select two.
questions.explanation: OVN-Kubernetes secondary networks for VMs support layer2 (overlay logical switch) and localnet (physical underlay, extra OVS config). Layer2 needs no extra physical fabric between nodes.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: A multihomed VM should keep pod-network NAT and also attach to a Linux bridge NAD named br-vlan. Which two stanza pairs belong in the VM spec? Select two.

choices.text: interfaces: masquerade: {} name: default  and  networks: name: default pod: {}
interfaces: bridge: {} name: vlan  and  networks: name: vlan multus.networkName: br-vlan
interfaces: masquerade: {} name: vlan  and  networks: name: vlan multus.networkName: br-vlan
spec.hostNetwork: true with no interfaces list

questions.explanation: Multihoming means two (or more) NICs. Default pod net uses masquerade + pod: {}. The secondary NAD uses bridge: {} and networks[].multus.networkName. Masquerade is invalid on the Multus/bridge NIC. hostNetwork is a pod field, not how VMs attach to NADs.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: In a VirtualMachine spec, how do you point a NIC at a NetworkAttachmentDefinition in another namespace?
questions.explanation: Each extra NIC is listed under domain.devices.interfaces and spec.template.spec.networks. For Multus, set multus.networkName to name or namespace/name of the NAD.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: You added a second NIC to a running VM’s VirtualMachine manifest. What documented virtctl step attaches that NIC?
questions.explanation: After editing the VM to add interfaces/networks, live-migrate with virtctl migrate so the new NIC is hot-plugged on the running VMI. Deleting the launcher pod is not the documented attach method.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: A VM needs a VF from an SR-IOV network already defined in the namespace. Which NIC type do you select?
questions.explanation: If an SR-IOV network is defined in the namespace, the NIC type is SR-IOV. Bridge is Linux-bridge NADs; masquerade is the default pod network. Do not pick a Service type as a NIC binding.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: Which virtctl command creates a Service that publishes SSH on a VM to the cluster’s load-balancer infrastructure?

choices.text: virtctl expose vm web1 --name web1-ssh --type LoadBalancer --port 22

questions.explanation: virtctl expose vm <vm> --name <svc> --type ClusterIP|NodePort|LoadBalancer --port <port> creates the Service. Routes are HTTP/TLS ingress, not a generic TCP 22 publish.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: Which two Service types can virtctl expose use besides ClusterIP? Select two.
questions.explanation: Documented expose types are ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer. LoadBalancer is the type used for external access via the cloud or metal LB. ExternalName is not in the virtctl expose list.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: Exposing a VM as a Kubernetes Service lets you use native load balancing so clients outside the cluster can reach a designated guest port.
questions.explanation: A Service object exposes the VM inside or outside the cluster. LoadBalancer type is the documented way to publish a VM port on the cluster’s load-balancer addresses.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: When you create a Service YAML by hand instead of virtctl expose, what must match so kube-proxy can select the VM’s pod?

choices.text: Service spec.selector labels and the VM template metadata labels (for example expose: me)
The Service name must equal the node hostname
The Service namespace must be openshift-ingress
The VM must use hostNetwork: true

questions.explanation: The Service selector must match labels on the VM template (copied to the virt-launcher pod). Documented examples use a label such as expose: me.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: What is the kind of the object you create to request a VM snapshot?
questions.explanation: VirtualMachineSnapshot (snapshot.kubevirt.io/v1beta1) is the user request. The controller also creates VirtualMachineSnapshotContent bound 1:1 to that snapshot.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: Which apiVersion is shown in the documented VirtualMachineSnapshot example?
questions.explanation: The VM snapshot CR uses snapshot.kubevirt.io/v1beta1. CSI VolumeSnapshot is snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1 (used under the hood). DataVolume is cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: In a VirtualMachineSnapshot spec.source stanza, which fields identify the VM?
questions.explanation: spec.source must name the VirtualMachine (apiGroup kubevirt.io). The snapshot then copies CSI volumes plus VM spec and metadata.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: Which two conditions must a disk meet to be included in a VM snapshot? Select two.

choices.text: It is a data volume or persistent volume claim
Its storage class supports CSI volume snapshots
It is a containerDisk stored only in a registry

questions.explanation: Included disks must be DVs or PVCs on a CSI snapshot-capable storage class, and they must be bound and populated. containerDisk and hostPath are not CSI snapshot sources.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: A VirtualMachineSnapshot can be edited after creation to add disks that were excluded.
questions.explanation: Snapshots cannot be changed after creation. You create a new snapshot if you need a different disk set.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: In the web console, where do you create a snapshot of an existing VM?
questions.explanation: Open Virtualization → VirtualMachines, select the VM, Snapshots tab, Take Snapshot. You can expand Disks included in this Snapshot before saving.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: What does restoring a VM from a snapshot do?

choices.text: Returns that existing VM to the disk and spec state captured in the snapshot
Creates a new VM from the snapshot without changing the source VM
Creates only a VolumeSnapshot of the PVC with no VM spec
Exports the VM with virtctl vmexport

questions.explanation: Restore rolls the existing VM back to the snapshot’s disks and spec. Creating a new VM from a snapshot is a separate Snapshots-tab action (Create VirtualMachine). VolumeSnapshot is the CSI object under the hood, not the restore result.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: Cloning a VM that has a vTPM device, or creating a new VM from that VM’s snapshot, is supported.
questions.explanation: Documented limitation: cloning a VM with a vTPM attached, or creating a new VM from its snapshot, is not supported.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: How do you clone a VM in the web console?

choices.text: VirtualMachine details → Actions → Clone, then name the new VM

questions.explanation: Actions → Clone opens Clone VirtualMachine. You name the clone and may check Start cloned VM. You can also create a VM from a snapshot via the Snapshots tab.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: To clone an existing VM disk PVC into a new volume with an independent lifecycle, which source does a DataVolume use?

choices.text: spec.source.pvc.namespace and spec.source.pvc.name of the original disk

questions.explanation: CDI DataVolume YAML clones with source.pvc namespace/name. The new DV’s lifecycle is independent of the original VM. virtctl create vm --volume-import type:pvc,src:ns/pvc can consume that clone.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: What kind (CDI API) represents an import or clone that must finish before the VM is allowed to start?
questions.explanation: DataVolume (cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1) is the CDI object for HTTP/registry/PVC import and clone. Data volumes prevent a VM from starting until the PVC is prepared.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: For CDI CSI volume cloning, which two requirements apply? Select two.

choices.text: Source and target PVCs use the same storage class and volume mode
The source volume must not be in use
The source must be an NFS export outside the cluster
The VM must be running with a vTPM

questions.explanation: CSI cloning needs matching storage class and volume mode, and the source volume must not be in use. You also need datavolumes/source permission in the source namespace. Smart cloning uses CSI snapshots instead when the plugin supports them.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: Which virtctl create vm option imports a qcow2 from an HTTP URL into a new disk?
questions.explanation: Documented HTTP import is virtctl create vm --volume-import type:http,url:<url>,size:<size>. Golden images in-cluster use type:ds,src:openshift-virtualization-os-images/<os>.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: Where do Red Hat-provided boot sources such as rhel9 typically live for --volume-import type:ds?
questions.explanation: Examples use type:ds,src:openshift-virtualization-os-images/rhel9. The catalog lists bootable volumes in that namespace that carry instancetype.kubevirt.io/default-preference.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: Which command creates a VirtualMachineExport so you can download a VM’s PVC?
questions.explanation: virtctl vmexport create <name> --vm|snapshot|pvc=<object> creates the export CR. Default TTL is 2 hours. download retrieves the volume; the CR is deleted after download unless --keep-vme.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: If you omit --ttl, how long does a VirtualMachineExport last by default? Enter a short form such as 2h.
questions.explanation: Optional --ttl=1h overrides TTL. The default duration is 2 hours.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: virtctl vmexport create can export volumes from which two of these sources (in addition to a raw PVC)? Select two.
questions.explanation: Create accepts --vm, --snapshot, or --pvc. Snapshot exports the PVCs stored in the VirtualMachineSnapshot. MachineSet and Ingress are unrelated.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: You need YAML that another cluster can use to import an exported disk. Which virtctl flag retrieves that manifest?
questions.explanation: vmexport download … --manifest returns the import manifest. It omits the header secret unless you also pass --include-secret. That secret grants access to the export endpoint.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: Which command hot-plugs an existing DataVolume or PVC onto a running VM?
questions.explanation: virtctl addvolume <vm> --volume-name=<dv_or_pvc> hot-plugs the volume. Optional --persist makes the disk permanent on the VM (not on a VMI-only object). --serial sets a label.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: The virtctl addvolume --persist flag permanently mounts the disk on a VirtualMachine. It does not apply to VirtualMachineInstance-only objects.
questions.explanation: Documentation: --persist mounts the virtual disk permanently on a VM. This flag does not apply to VMIs.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: Which virtctl subcommand hot-unplugs a virtual disk? Enter the subcommand only.
questions.explanation: virtctl removevolume <vm_name> --volume-name=<virtual_disk> hot-unplugs the disk.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: In the create/customize wizard, which tab do you use to add or review VM disks before clicking Create VirtualMachine?
questions.explanation: Customize VirtualMachine includes Overview, YAML, Scheduling, Environment, Network interfaces, Disks, Scripts, and Metadata. Disks is where you attach storage. You can also add a volume from Catalog with Add volume (upload, existing PVC, snapshot, or containerDisk).

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: You must install the QEMU guest agent on VMs created from operating system images that are not provided by Red Hat.
questions.explanation: When cloning PVCs with custom images, documentation requires the QEMU guest agent on guests that did not come from Red Hat OS images.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Why would you run virtctl start --paused web1?

choices.text: So you can interrupt the boot process from the VNC console
To force a CSI snapshot before the guest starts
To bind the VM to the default MachineSet

questions.explanation: virtctl start --paused starts the VM paused so you can break into firmware/boot from VNC. It is not a snapshot or MachineSet operation.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which virtctl invocation force-stops a VM and is documented as a possible cause of data loss?
questions.explanation: virtctl stop <vm> --grace-period 0 --force is the documented force stop. It may cause inconsistency or data loss. pause keeps state in RAM instead of powering off.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which virtctl subcommand reboots a virtual machine? Enter the subcommand only.
questions.explanation: virtctl restart <vm_name> restarts the guest. stop then start is a two-step alternative; restart is the dedicated command.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two virtctl commands start or cancel a live migration? Select two.
questions.explanation: virtctl migrate starts live migration; virtctl migrate-cancel aborts it. vmexport is disk export, not migration.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: You want a graphical console from the CLI. Which command is documented, and what local tool does it need?

choices.text: virtctl vnc web1 — virt-viewer must be installed

questions.explanation: virtctl vnc connects to the VNC console and requires virt-viewer. --proxy-only=true prints a port so you can attach any VNC client. virtctl console is serial, not graphical.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: A guest already has your public key. Which two virtctl commands use the matching private key with -i? Select two.
questions.explanation: virtctl ssh and virtctl scp take -i <private_key> and user@vm. The VM must already have the public key. expose and addvolume are unrelated.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two virtctl commands report guest-agent facts from a running VM? Select two.
questions.explanation: guestosinfo shows guest OS data; userlist shows logged-in users; fslist shows filesystems. All need the guest agent. create instancetype writes a sizing CR.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: On RHEL 9 you want the virtctl binary from the cluster UI. Where is Download virtctl?
questions.explanation: The Virtualization Overview page has Download virtctl for your OS. RHEL 8 can use the kubevirt-virtctl RPM instead.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which two fields are required on a VirtualMachineInstancetype spec? Select two.
questions.explanation: cpu.guest (vCPU count) and memory.guest are required. Other VirtualMachineInstancetypeSpec fields are optional. virtctl create instancetype --cpu 2 --memory 256Mi fills both.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: Which one-liner creates a cluster-wide instance type object immediately?
questions.explanation: virtctl create instancetype prints YAML; piping to oc apply creates the object. --namespace makes it namespaced instead of cluster-wide.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: Which common-instancetypes series is memory-intensive (hugepages, burstable CPU, 1:8 vCPU-to-memory)?
questions.explanation: M is memory intensive: hugepages, burstable CPU, 1:8 ratio; m1.large is 2 vCPU / 16 GiB. U is general purpose 1:4; N is network/DPDK; O is overcommitted.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: You clicked Customize VirtualMachine. Which tab holds Cloud-init, SSH key, or Windows Sysprep settings that must be set before first boot?
questions.explanation: The Scripts tab is where you edit Cloud-init, SSH key, or Sysprep (Windows) before the VM boots. Scheduling is node placement; Metadata is labels/annotations.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: When customizing a Windows boot volume in the catalog, which two answer-file names can you attach for Sysprep? Select two.
questions.explanation: The Windows Sysprep UI takes Autoattend.xml and Unattend.xml. virtctl create vm --volume-sysprep also requires unattend.xml or autounattend.xml in a ConfigMap. Kickstart and cloud-init are Linux.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: When creating a Windows VM you can select Mount Windows drivers disk so virtio drivers are available in the guest.
questions.explanation: Customize VirtualMachine → Storage includes Mount Windows drivers disk. The template catalog has the same checkbox for Windows templates.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: In VirtualMachine details while creating a Linux VM, you add an SSH public key and tick Automatically apply this key to any new VirtualMachine you create in this project. What does that do?

choices.text: Stores the key as a project secret reused for later VMs in that namespace
Adds the key only to this VM and does not create a reusable secret
Writes the key into every node’s authorized_keys
Stores the key in kube-system for all projects

questions.explanation: You can Use existing or Add new for Authorized SSH key. Add new can save the secret and optionally apply it to new VMs in the project.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: The catalog create wizard can show both the VirtualMachine YAML and the equivalent CLI commands before you click Create VirtualMachine.
questions.explanation: View YAML & CLI lets you inspect, copy, or download the YAML or the CLI commands generated for the VM you are about to create.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: How do you tell virtctl create vm to use a namespaced instance type rather than a cluster-wide one?
questions.explanation: Include the namespaced kind: --instancetype virtualmachineinstancetype/<name>. Bare --instancetype <name> or virtualmachineclusterinstancetype/<name> selects the cluster-wide object. --preference is a different resource.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: You need an interactive libguestfs-tools container attached to a PVC to inspect a disk. Which command is documented?
questions.explanation: virtctl guestfs -n <ns> <pvc> deploys libguestfs-tools with that PVC mounted. The PVC name is required. Do not start a VM that uses the same PVC while guestfs is running.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: A virtctl-generated VM YAML shows runStrategy: Always. What does that mean after you oc apply it?

choices.text: The control plane keeps a VirtualMachineInstance running (start on create, restart if it stops)
The VM is created but left off (same as runStrategy: Halted)
Live migration is disabled for this VM
Instance types on the VM are ignored

questions.explanation: runStrategy Always is the documented generated default in several virtctl create vm examples: the VM is started and kept running. Halted/Manual/RerunOnFailure are other strategies.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: A copied VM template is marked deprecated after an SSP Operator update. Which two labels should you remove to clear the base-template mark? Select two.
questions.explanation: Remove template.kubevirt.io/type=base and template.kubevirt.io/version, then remove the template.kubevirt.io/deprecated annotation. Those identify SSP base templates.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What apiVersion is used on a NetworkAttachmentDefinition manifest?
questions.explanation: NADs are k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1 NetworkAttachmentDefinition objects. UserDefinedNetwork uses k8s.ovn.org/v1 instead.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What apiVersion is used on a UserDefinedNetwork custom resource?
questions.explanation: UDN and ClusterUserDefinedNetwork are k8s.ovn.org/v1. Do not name the UDN default or collide with CNO global namespaces.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: Which two role values can a UserDefinedNetwork spec use? Select two.
questions.explanation: UDN role is Primary (replaces default pod network in a labeled namespace) or Secondary (extra network). NodePort is a Service type; masquerade is a KubeVirt binding.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: On a UserDefinedNetwork, which topology does not provide persistent IP addresses for VMs?

choices.text: Layer2 with a shared OVN logical switch
A Linux-bridge NAD (not a UDN topology)

questions.explanation: The UDN support matrix: Layer2 has persistent IPs; Layer3 does not. Layer2 is the topology recommended for VM live migration without NAT. Linux-bridge NADs are a different attachment method, not a UDN topology value.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: An OVN-Kubernetes layer2 secondary network connects VMs on different nodes using which overlay protocol?
questions.explanation: OVN-Kubernetes uses Geneve to build the layer2 overlay logical switch. VMs on different nodes talk without extra physical L2 fabric. localnet is the topology that hits the underlay instead.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: A Linux-bridge NetworkAttachmentDefinition created in the web console should live in the same namespace as the VM or pod that will attach to it.
questions.explanation: The NAD create wizard notes that the definition must be in the same namespace as the pod or VM. You can still reference namespace/name from VM YAML when the NAD is elsewhere.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: What does documentation call the most efficient method for connecting a VM to a VLAN?

choices.text: A Linux bridge network attachment definition
A masquerade NIC on the default pod network

questions.explanation: A Linux bridge NAD is documented as the most efficient way to connect a VM to a VLAN. Services and Ingress publish application ports; they are not L2 VLAN attachment.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: In a Linux-bridge NAD spec.config JSON, which CNI type attaches the VM tap to a node bridge?
questions.explanation: OpenShift 4.18 Linux-bridge NAD examples set spec.config type to bridge (web console Network Type: CNV Linux bridge). ovn-k8s-cni-overlay is the OVN secondary NAD type; ipvlan and macvlan are other CNI plugins used with NADs, not the Linux-bridge VM path.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: A VM has spec.hostname myvm and spec.subdomain mysubdomain in namespace apps. What internal FQDN does documentation describe?
questions.explanation: Internal FQDN format is <hostname>.<subdomain>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local. A matching headless Service is used so that name resolves.

questions.objective: Configure external access with load balancer services
questions.stem: You ran virtctl expose vm web1 --name web1-ssh --type NodePort --port 22. How do clients reach SSH on the guest?

choices.text: Each node IP on the allocated NodePort
A cloud or metal load-balancer hostname (LoadBalancer type)
An OpenShift Route listening on TCP 22

questions.explanation: NodePort publishes the Service on a port on every node. LoadBalancer would allocate an external LB address instead. OpenShift Routes are HTTP/TLS, not arbitrary TCP 22. virtctl console is serial, not SSH.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: A VM NIC using masquerade on the pod network is expected to obtain its IPv4 address via DHCP.
questions.explanation: Masquerade-mode docs require the guest to use DHCP for IPv4. The examples are written that way. Dual-stack masquerade is a separate documented option.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: You are customizing a VM in the web console and need a second NIC. Which tab do you use?
questions.explanation: Customize VirtualMachine includes a Network interfaces tab. You can add NICs now or later; a VM can be created with no NIC and get one afterwards.

questions.objective: Configure multihomed virtual machines
questions.stem: Which NIC model is listed alongside e1000e as a supported value in OpenShift Virtualization networking fields?
questions.explanation: Documented NIC models include e1000e and virtio (older pages also list e1000, ne2k_pci, pcnet, rtl8139). virtio is the usual paravirtual choice.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: Pods on the default network must reach a VM on a primary UDN on UDP/53. Which annotation opens that port on the UDN endpoint?
questions.explanation: k8s.ovn.org/open-default-ports lists protocol/port pairs. Those ports are reachable on the default-network IP of the UDN pod/VM, not on the UDN IP.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: After you create a VirtualMachineSnapshot, which related object does the snapshot controller bind 1:1 to it?
questions.explanation: The snapshot feature adds VirtualMachineSnapshot, VirtualMachineSnapshotContent, and related CRDs. Content is bound 1:1 to the Snapshot the user created.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: You can create a VirtualMachineSnapshot for either an online (running) VM or an offline VM.
questions.explanation: CLI docs: create a snapshot for an offline or online VM by creating a VirtualMachineSnapshot object. Online snapshots can be verified with snapshot indications.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: On the Snapshots tab of a VM, which action creates a new VM from an existing snapshot instead of restoring the original?
questions.explanation: Create VirtualMachine on a snapshot copies that point-in-time disk/spec into a new VM. Restore applies the snapshot back onto the source VM. vTPM snapshots cannot be used this way.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: After virtctl vmexport download, the VirtualMachineExport CR is deleted by default. Which flag keeps it?
questions.explanation: --keep-vme retains the export CR after download. --insecure allows HTTP. --persist belongs to addvolume, not vmexport.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: virtctl vmexport download export --manifest omits a credential by default. Which extra flag includes the header secret in the manifest?
questions.explanation: The export manifest does not include the header secret unless you pass --include-secret. That secret authorizes the import endpoint.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: When downloading an exported volume, which flag sets the output file (example disk.img.gz)?
questions.explanation: virtctl vmexport download <export> --output=<file> --volume=<name> writes the volume. --volume is optional if the export has only one volume.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: Which component (full name or CDI) chooses CSI clone vs smart clone when you create a DataVolume from a PVC?
questions.explanation: The Containerized Data Importer (CDI) implements DataVolumes and picks CSI volume cloning or smart cloning (clone via CSI snapshot) based on the storage profile.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: What is smart cloning in CDI?

choices.text: Create a PVC from a CSI volume snapshot, then clone further PVCs efficiently from that snapshot
Copy disk bytes through virtctl scp
Live-migrate the VM onto the clone
Rebuild the qcow2 with virt-sysprep only

questions.explanation: When the CSI plugin supports snapshots, CDI can snapshot the source and provision the target PVC from that snapshot. Direct CSI volume cloning is the other efficient path.

questions.objective: Import previously exported virtual machines
questions.stem: You already cloned a disk into PVC my-project/imported-volume-q5pr9. Which virtctl create vm import type consumes it?
questions.explanation: --volume-import type:pvc,src:<ns>/<pvc> is the documented clone-from-PVC form. HTTP is for URLs; ds is for DataSources such as openshift-virtualization-os-images/rhel9.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: From Virtualization → Catalog, Add volume can source a bootable volume from which two of these (besides upload and containerDisk)? Select two.
questions.explanation: Add volume uploads a new image or uses an existing PVC, a volume snapshot, or a containerDisk. The question already excludes upload and containerDisk from the two answers, so PVC and volume snapshot are the pair. A DataSource in another project is a virtctl --volume-import type:ds path, not an Add volume source listed in that dialog.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: virtctl addvolume web1 --volume-name=data1 --serial=logs-disk does what with --serial?

choices.text: Sets a label on the VM disk; default label is the DataVolume or PVC name
Enables serial console instead of VNC

questions.explanation: --serial=<label> labels the hot-plugged disk. If omitted, the DV/PVC name is used. It is not related to virtctl console.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: A DataVolume listed in a VM’s dataVolumeTemplates keeps the VM from starting until the PVC is fully prepared.
questions.explanation: Data volumes prevent a VM from starting before the PVC is prepared. That is why imports and clones are modeled as DataVolumes rather than raw PVCs alone.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: The web-console Clone VirtualMachine dialog can optionally start the cloned VM immediately.
questions.explanation: After Actions → Clone you name the new VM and may select Start cloned VM, then click Clone.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: The Take Snapshot wizard warns that some disks cannot be included. How do you continue anyway?

choices.text: Select I am aware of this warning and wish to proceed, then Save
Uncheck the ineligible disks and Save, with no warning checkbox
Change the disk storage class, then retry Take Snapshot
Stop the VM; online snapshots cannot continue with excluded disks

questions.explanation: You can expand Disks included in this Snapshot, acknowledge the warning if some disks are ineligible, and Save. Ineligible disks stay out of that snapshot.

questions.objective: Attach storage to virtual machines
questions.stem: What apiVersion is used on a DataVolume manifest in the documented PVC-clone example?
questions.explanation: DataVolume YAML uses apiVersion cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1. VirtualMachine remains kubevirt.io/v1; snapshots use snapshot.kubevirt.io/v1beta1.

questions.objective: Create clones for virtual machines
questions.stem: Inside a virtctl guestfs session you want to seal a disk image so it can be used as a template. Which libguestfs command is listed?
questions.explanation: virtctl guestfs documents virt-sysprep -a /dev/vda to seal a VM disk as a template. Other virt-* tools can edit files, inject SSH keys, or show disk usage.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: In the Administrator view, where do you create a namespace-scoped UserDefinedNetwork?
questions.explanation: Create UserDefinedNetwork from Networking → UserDefinedNetworks, pick the labeled project, and set topology/role/subnets. The namespace must already have k8s.ovn.org/primary-user-defined-network if the UDN is primary.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the command line interface (CLI)
questions.stem: A VM was paused with virtctl pause vm web1. Which virtctl subcommand resumes it? Enter the subcommand only.
questions.explanation: virtctl unpause vm <vm_name> resumes a paused VM whose state was kept in memory.

questions.objective: Provision and manage virtual machines from the web interface
questions.stem: Which common-instancetypes series is compute-exclusive (hugepages, dedicated CPU, isolated emulator threads, vNUMA, 1:2 ratio)?
questions.explanation: CX is Compute Exclusive: hugepages, dedicated CPU, isolated emulator threads, vNUMA, 1:2. cx1.2xlarge is 8 vCPU / 16 GiB. N is the network/DPDK cousin.

questions.objective: Create and manage snapshots for virtual machines
questions.stem: Besides DV/PVC and CSI snapshot support, which two volume states are required for a disk to join a VM snapshot? Select two.
questions.explanation: Snapshot-eligible disks must be bound PVs and populated from a datasource, in addition to being DV/PVC on CSI snapshot storage. Size and hostPath are not those criteria.

questions.objective: Connect virtual machines to predefined networks, such as user-defined networks
questions.stem: When would you choose OVN-Kubernetes localnet instead of layer2 for a VM secondary network?

choices.text: You need the secondary network connected to the physical underlay (east-west and outside the cluster), and you can configure OVS on nodes
You only need an overlay with no underlay changes
You must use masquerade on that NIC
You want persistent IPs without extra OVS work and no physical access

questions.explanation: localnet attaches the secondary network to the physical underlay and needs extra OVS configuration. layer2 is the overlay logical switch (Geneve) when you do not want extra physical fabric.
